summary: WorldEntity generation-5 still permits a caller-controlled effectively unbounded duplicate-diagnostic history. createRegistry() validates duplicateDiagnosticCapacity only as a non-negative safe integer, so values up to 9007199254740991 are accepted and the registry retains duplicate diagnostics until that caller-supplied capacity. The default 64 and ring-eviction logic are bounded only when callers choose a practical value. This violates the project-owned bounded-cache/queue requirement. Current tests prove capacity=2 eviction, capacity=0 disablement, and rejection of math.huge, but do not reject an impractically large finite capacity. Recommended bounded follow-up: introduce an explicit project maximum diagnostic capacity, reject values above it, preserve default/zero/small behavior, and add exact boundary regressions. Do not spawn an overlapping implementation while the current WorldEntity primary/resource is live; route this into the retained successor lineage or a later non-overlapping one-shot after ownership is clear.
evidence: PR #397 exact head 83850e9f2bab4572de800428fb510b6b75fc2c45: createRegistry() feeds duplicateDiagnosticCapacity through assertNonNegativeInteger, whose ceiling is MAX_SAFE_INTEGER=9007199254740991.
The duplicate ring evicts only when #duplicates >= capacity, so a huge finite caller capacity removes the practical memory bound even though the default is 64.
tests/world_entity.luau covers capacity 2, capacity 0, and math.huge rejection but has no finite project-maximum boundary regression.
Repository/issue search found no existing duplicateDiagnosticCapacity maximum or dedicated bounded-capacity issue/lane.

metadata.recommendedDisposition: absorb into retained WorldEntity successor when ownership is available
